title: control-plane-raft-lag-regional-failover-recovery-diary
content:
Executive summary:

On 2024-11-01 01:12 UTC we observed a gradual increase in schedule failures and API latency in region eu-west-2. Symptoms escalated over ~20 minutes into a partial regional control-plane degradation: the kube-scheduler began deferring pods (Pending p95 increased from 200ms to ~4s), and API server p95 rose from 40ms to 800ms. Control-plane metrics showed increased etcd raft apply latency and leader election churn.

Impact:
- Pods in eu-west-2 hit Pending spikes; some stateful workloads briefly failed readiness probes and restarted (~120 restarts across 3 node pools).
- Cluster autoscaler misbehaved due to delayed Pod scheduling decisions for 12 minutes.
- No customer data loss; API responded eventually.

Detection timeline (approx):
- 01:12 UTC: Alert: kube-scheduler Pending pods p95 > 1s (alert SRE-POD-SCHED-12).
- 01:14 UTC: API p95 alert fired (SRE-API-LATENCY-7).
- 01:15 UTC: Pager escalation; on-call started triage. Initial theory: transient API server overload.
- 01:18 UTC: Observed etcd raft-apply-latency metric rising; etcd leader CPU normal but etcd apply queues growing.
- 01:22 UTC: Noted sustained disk latency (iostat: avg await 100-300ms) on control-plane nodes; network jitter also elevated across the AZ.
- 01:30 UTC: Control-plane leader moved (raft leader election). Scheduling P95 started to recover as leader stabilized on a healthier control-plane node.
- 01:40 UTC: Primary mitigations completed, alerts resolved by ~02:00 UTC.

Investigation notes and commands run (raw):
- kubectl get componentstatuses && kubectl get pods -n kube-system -o wide -- showed apiserver, controller-manager, scheduler pods running but with occasional 500s in apiserver logs.
- journalctl -u etcd -f on control-plane-2 revealed repeated "raft: declined MsgVote" followed by "raft: leader changed" entries.
- etcdctl --endpoints=https://10.2.3.11:2379 endpoint status returned high "raftAppliedIndex" gaps between nodes and increased server_timeouts.
- iostat -x 1 10 on control-plane-2: avg await 220ms. blkio showed large bursts matching the time window.
- tcpdump on control-plane network interface showed retransmits and bursts consistent with packet drops (interface saturated by backups).
- cloud provider console: ~01:00-01:30 UTC background snapshot jobs ran on control-plane host EBS volumes in the region (snapshots of etcd backup + daily image backups).

Root cause hypothesis (evidence-based):
Primary cause: I/O interference on control-plane hosts during simultaneous snapshot jobs. On control-plane-2, scheduled snapshots caused prolonged EBS read/write latency spikes which increased etcd raft apply latency. Raft leader elections occurred when a follower's heartbeat latency exceeded election timeout, causing transient leader changes and a period where apply throughput dropped.
Contributing factors:
- No isolation between backup snapshot IO and control-plane etcd volume (snapshots run on same hosts/volumes during a maintenance window).
- Alerts for disk IO latency on control-plane were missing or set with a high threshold (avg await >500ms).
- Cluster autoscaler and scheduler have limited backoff for transient API errors, amplifying visible customer impact.

Immediate mitigations performed during incident:
- Disabled in-flight snapshot jobs for the region (~01:28 UTC) through provider console -> reduced IO pressure.
- Forced stable etcd leader by cordoning control-plane-2 from being leader candidate (temporary config tweak) until snapshot jobs completed.
- Throttled backup schedule globally for control-plane buckets to avoid overlap with peak hours and control-plane maintenance windows.

Commands used for mitigation (kept for runbook):
- cloud-provider snapshot cancel --region eu-west-2 --job-id <id>
- kubectl get pods -n kube-system -o wide # identify control-plane components
- ssh control-plane-2 sudo systemctl stop backup-agent.service # (temporal)
- kubectl patch configmap kubeadm-config -n kube-system --type merge -p '{"data":{"apiServerExtraArgs":"--initial-cluster-state=existing"}}' # example (note: use safer method in runbook)

Post-incident root cause confirmation steps performed:
- Replayed snapshot schedule logs and matched I/O bursts to etcd apply latency spikes.
- Recreated a small-scale test: forced snapshot on a control-plane volume under synthetic load; observed similar raft apply stalls and transient elections in test cluster.

Runbook draft changes (actionable items to add/edit):
1) Control-plane IO isolation: enforce backups/snapshots to use separate volumes or off-host snapshot proxy for control-plane etcd volumes. Add a runbook section: "How to cancel / throttle provider snapshots" with exact UI/API commands for GCP/AWS/Azure.
2) Alerting: add alerts for control-plane disk await > 50ms sustained over 1m and > 150ms over 5m, and etcd raft_apply_latency > 100ms for 1m. Current thresholds were too permissive.
3) Leader-election protection: add guidance to prefer fast-fail backup operations (throttle vs cancel) and a temporary leader-avoid annotation we can apply during noisy maintenance windows. Document kubectl and admission controller steps.
4) Backup scheduling policy: Central policy to avoid scheduling host-level snapshots on nodes tagged control-plane during 00:00-06:00 UTC; schedule backups to control-plane volumes via managed snapshot service that uses copy-on-write without burst IO.
5) Scheduler resiliency tweak: add backoff improvements in cluster autoscaler config to reduce churn when apiserver p95 > 500ms.

Follow-ups (owners + ETA):
- SRE-Infra: implement snapshot isolation for etcd volumes (Owner: Priya Nambiar) - ETA 2024-12-01.
- Monitoring: add disk await + raft apply alerts (Owner: Ethan Zhao) - ETA 2024-11-10.
- Platform: update backup job orchestration to respect "control-plane-protected" tag (Owner: Mariana Ortiz) - ETA 2024-11-24.
- Runbook: merge this incident notes into control-plane-runbook.md and add step-by-step cancellation commands (Owner: Jordan Kim) - ETA 2024-11-08.

Notes for future on-call triage (short checklist to put in runbook):
- Step 0: On alert, verify if region has scheduled provider backups (cloud console API check).
- Step 1: Check etcd metrics: raft_apply_latency, leader_changes, proposal_queue_length.
- Step 2: Check host IO: iostat, sar, dstat; look for avg await >50ms sustained.
- Step 3: If IO issue present, consider cancelling/throttling backups and cordoning backup agent.
- Step 4: If leader flaps persist, temporarily mark unhealthy control-plane node as non-voter via etcdctl or move leader (careful, follow detailed steps).
- Step 5: Post-mitigation, run a controlled leader election test on a staging cluster before re-enabling backups.

Artifacts to attach to postmortem (links):
- Cloud snapshot job logs and IDs (attached to JIRA-SRE-4823).
- etcd logs (control-plane-1/2/3) compressed and uploaded to artifact store.
- Test script used to recreate condition: scripts/etcd-snapshot-io-test.sh (repo: platform/tools).

Open questions remaining:
- Why did provider snapshot service cause such large synchronous IO rather than offloading (probe provider team).
- Should we maintain a dedicated control-plane snapshot window vs fully disallow host snapshots? (ops policy decision).
- Could we add a lightweight leader-protection admission controller that blocks leader elections during scheduled maintenance? (design discussion).

Appendix: misc logs & snippets (sanitized)
- etcd log excerpt: "2024-11-01T01:17:22Z etcdserver: applied entry at index 1234567: took 0.421s (raft_apply_latency)"
- iostat snippet: "sda  rrqm/s wrqm/s r/s w/s rkB/s wkB/s avgrq-sz avgqu-sz await r_await w_await svctm %util
  0.00 0.00 1.00 300.00 8.00 20480.00 15.20 12.50 220.30 0.12 220.18 0.50 95.00"

Triage notes (less formal, left from on-call):
- "At first thought apiserver CPU, but CPU normal. Jumped to etcd after seeing apply queue. Control-plane-2 had huge disk await spikes and backup agent running. Cancelling snapshot immediately helped. If only we had a disk await alert earlier."
